# The deck pipeline

**Workflow:** [`tarot/tarot-deck-pipeline.json`](../tarot/tarot-deck-pipeline.json)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | `tarot` |
| Nodes | 14 |
| Links | 17 |
| Paid API calls per run | **1 per input** |
| Reads | `tarot/base` |
| Writes | `tarot/deck-out` |

---

Base art in, a finished deck out. Every position in the deck is a slot; the pipeline runs once per slot and nothing downstream needs to know which card it is holding.

**Deck Manifest → Slot Loader → Prompt Builder → generate → Frame → Lettering → Save**

## Read this before spending anything

`scope` on the manifest starts at **major arcana (22)**. Set it to `full deck (78)` only once a run has come out the way you want, because that is 78 API calls. There is no partial billing.

## 1 · Deck Manifest — the shape of the deck

78 slots in order, each carrying its own title, numeral, suit, rank and element. `tradition` sets the names: `rws`, `marseille` or `thoth` (both of the latter seat Justice at VIII and Strength at XI). For a deck of your own, `suit_names` and `court_names` take four comma-separated names each, and `custom_titles` takes one title per line in deck order — so *Tarot of the Hidden Light* can carry its own vocabulary while every other node still knows what position it is on.

## 2 · Slot Loader — where your art meets the slots

Point `directory` at your base images. Filenames are matched by name, not by order, so all of these land on the right slot:

`the-fool.png` · `03-empress.png` · `HighPriestess_final.png` · `XVI_the_tower.png` · `wands_07.png` · `SevenOfCups_v2.png` · `queen-of-swords.png`

Then read the **report** output. It names every file it matched and to what, every file it could not place, and every slot still empty. Read it before you queue anything — a misfiled card is much cheaper to catch here.

`on_missing` = **blank slot** is deliberate for a deck in progress: an unfilled position stays in the run holding a labelled placeholder, so the contact sheet at the end shows the whole deck with its gaps rather than a shorter deck that hides them. Switch to `skip` to spend nothing on the gaps, or `error` to refuse to run until the deck is complete.

`overrides` is the escape hatch — one `slug = filename` per line for anything the matcher gets wrong.

## 3 · Prompt Builder — the same instruction, per card

`{title}` `{numeral}` `{arcana}` `{suit}` `{rank}` `{element}` `{slug}` `{index}` `{style}`

`style` is the one block you retune between whole-deck runs. The template is the sentence that stays fixed. Keeping them apart is the point: change `style` and every card changes together, consistently.

## 4 · Generate — art in, art out

Each card's own image goes into `input_image` and the style reference into `input_image_2`; the prompt names which is which. `disable_pup` is on so your prompt is used as written.

**Fix the seed.** A fixed seed makes the whole run reproducible *and* cacheable — if you then only change the frame or the lettering, re-queuing costs nothing at all, because every generate call comes back from the cache. This is what makes the border and title stages free to iterate on. Set the seed to -1 only when you want a genuinely different draw.

## 5 · Frame — the card as an object

Trim size at a real DPI, plus bleed. `tarot 2.75x4.75in` is the standard 70×120mm stock; set `bleed_mm` to 3 if a printer asked for it, 0 for screen.

`margin_pct` is the border band, as a percentage of card width. `top_margin_extra_pct` and `bottom_margin_extra_pct` open up the head and foot for the numeral and the title — the art box shrinks to make room, so the lettering never sits on the illustration.

`border_style`: `none`, `keyline`, `solid band`, `double rule`, `inset panel`. Or leave it `none` and put a border you designed elsewhere into `overlay_path` — any PNG with alpha, laid over the finished card at card size.

## 6 · Lettering — the name and the numeral

`title` and `numeral` come in from the loader, so each card is lettered with its own and the numerals stay aligned even when slots were skipped.

**Set `font_path`.** Blank falls back to Pillow's built-in face, which is fine for placing the block and not fine for print. Point it at a .ttf or .otf.

`tracking_px` is real letter-spacing — display lettering wants some, and Pillow has no such parameter, so the text is laid out a glyph at a time to provide it. Sizes are percentages of card height, so they hold when you change the trim size.

## 7 · Save — under the card's own name

`{index:02d}_{label}` with the slugs wired to `label` gives `00_the-fool.png`, `01_the-magician.png` … in deck order, which is what a print house wants and what you will want in six months.

`save_sidecar_json` is on: prompt, model, seed and size land beside each card as JSON, so any card can be traced back to what made it.

## 8 · Contact sheet — the whole deck at once

The sheet node sees the entire set rather than one card at a time, so this is where you judge whether a *deck* holds together — which is a different question from whether a card is good.
